answer: Key-bound sequential delay proofs withhold a seat's trading rights until it finishes its own serial delay chain. The chain starts only after the epoch seed appears, takes about 20 minutes on one core, and is locked to that seat's key. That proof later lets the seat grade a timber lot, book a dawn berth, or price a copper cathode, but it will not verify under another key, and extra processors cannot skip steps because each digest needs the last one. So 80 fake identities occupy 80 cores for 20 minutes every epoch; lining them up on one core takes more than 26 hours and they miss the window.
